hints: Look at what is building up in the soil. What does adding more dissolved salt do to the water potential of the soil solution?
Remember water always moves by osmosis from higher water potential to lower water potential. If soil becomes more salty than the root cells, which way must water move?
walkthrough:
**What salt does to soil water**

More dissolved salt means more solute particles. This lowers (makes more negative) the water potential of the soil solution. So the change is in the soil, not in the roots to start with.

**Which way will water move?**

Water moves by osmosis from higher water potential to lower water potential.

Normally: $soil (higher) \rightarrow root (lower)$ so roots absorb water.

With salty soil: $root (higher) \rightarrow soil (lower)$ so water is drawn out.

**Why the plant dies**

When water leaves the root cells instead of entering, the plant cannot replace water lost by transpiration. Cells lose turgor, wilt, and the plant eventually dies from physiological drought. That matches only option C.

options.A: Incorrect because the salt builds up in the soil, not in the roots, and water moving into the roots would help the plant, not kill it.
options.B: Incorrect because the key change is a decrease in soil water potential, not an increase in root water potential.
options.C: Correct because salty soil has decreased water potential, so water moves out of the roots into the soil by osmosis and the plant dies from water loss.
options.D: Incorrect because increased soil water potential would favour movement into the roots, which would not kill the crop.
